raw_response:
I don't know how to read or write, but I know my land. I've been farming these 10 mu and a bit — 10.1 mu to be exact — for 15 years now, since I was 21. My father taught me, and his father taught him. My wife works the fields with me, and my younger brother works in a factory in Shijiazhuang, but he comes back for planting and harvest. Between us and the three kids and my old mother, there's six mouths to feed, so every yuan I spend on the field is a yuan I can't spend at the clinic or at school.

It's October now, time to put in the winter wheat. I always keep my own seed — saved about 800 jin of good plump grain from last year, so I don't need to buy any. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the kind with the three numbers on it, then run the rotary tiller twice to mix it in. Last year fertilizer was so expensive I only used two-thirds of a bag, and the wheat came up thin. I regretted it. This year I'm going back to the full bag, and in the spring when the wheat turns green I'll spread half a bag of urea on top. Better to spend the money than risk a bad crop. My neighbor Old Wang does the same and his wheat always looks greener than mine.

For water, I pump from our tube well. Electricity is costly though. I'll water the wheat three times if it's dry — once after planting if the sky stays clear, once around Qingming when it starts shooting up, and once when the heads come out. But if heaven sends rain, I skip and save the money.

Come June, the wheat comes off and there's no time to breathe. I hire the combine — 50 yuan a mu — and that same week we plant maize. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town, the yellow bags, about 4 jin per mu, costs me around 40 yuan. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer in the holes when planting, and when the maize is knee-high I side-dress half a bag of urea. Maize needs water too, especially in July, so I'll pump once or twice depending on the rains.

I don't spray much poison. For wheat, if I see too many weeds in spring I might spray herbicide once. For maize, I drop those red insecticide granules in the planting hole to keep the worms off. My wife worries about chemicals with the kids around.

Most work we do ourselves. I might hire two village fellows for a day each during harvest if my brother can't make it back in time — 100 yuan a day plus lunch. For maize harvest we do it by hand, then hire the thresher.

If the weather is normal, I expect about 400 kg of wheat per mu and maybe 500 kg of maize. That'll give us enough to eat and some to sell. All told, I'll spend about 4,000 yuan on inputs this year, which is most of the cash I have, but what else can I do? The land has to produce.
